title: What If Every Virus on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every virus on Earth vanished? You'd think the planet would breathe easier.
In the ocean alone, there are about ten million viruses in every milliliter of seawater.
Most infect bacteria and plankton, and together they kill about twenty percent of the ocean's microbes every single day.
That killing recycles nutrients. By one estimate, up to a quarter of what plankton produce passes through this loop.
Viruses also help end harmful algal blooms, the red tides that can kill fish.
Take them away and the ocean loses one of its biggest recyclers. The invisible killers keep the sea in balance.
